claims.statement: For all integers t,k>=1, the genuine Boolean shared-address function F_{t,k}(x,y)=product_{r=1}^k y_{r,x} has a uniform spectral law on 2^(2t) atoms, H(F_{t,k})=2t and I(F_{t,k})=t/2+k. Its exact collision terms are B_W=M_W=t. It admits a lossless packet cover whose selector fractional spectral congestion is 1/2 although its unweighted worst-case read is 2^t. Meanwhile sum_i h2(I_i)=t+k2^t h2(2^-t), so with k=t that coordinatewise budget divided by influence diverges while H/I=4/3.
claims.quantifiers: All integers t,k>=1; all selector and data coordinates are fair and mutually independent; every data coordinate y_{r,b} is physically distinct.
scope_exclusions: Not a proof or counterexample for full FEI.
The family has positive selector energy I_sel/t=1/2 and is inside the existing closure.
Does not prove a universal cheap packet representation.
Does not control the unrestricted signed-dictator embedding.
refutes: Universal coordinatewise marginal-entropy estimate sum_i h2(I_i(f)) <= C I(f) for fixed finite C
